results.problem: Longest Common Subsequence over k-ary alphabet
results.bound: $(1/k + \epsilon_k)$-approximation in truly subquadratic time, conditional on a $(1/2 + \epsilon)$-approximation for binary LCS
results.quote: Theorem 1. For any fixed integer $k\ge 2$ there is an $O(n)$ time algorithm that given an instance of LCS for strings of length at most $n$ over an alphabet of size $k$, reduces it to $O(k^2)$ instances of LCS over binary strings of length at most $n$, so that $(1/2+\epsilon)$-approximate solutions (for $\epsilon>0$) for these LCS instances can be translated in $O(n)$ time into a $(1/k+\epsilon_k)$ approximation of the $k$-ary alphabet LCS instance, where $\epsilon_k>0$ is a constant only depending on $\epsilon$ and $k$.

results.problem: Longest Common Subsequence over k-ary alphabet
results.quote: Theorem 2. Given two strings $A$ and $B$ of length $n$ over an arbitrary alphabet of size $k$, there exist positive constants $\epsilon$ and $\delta$ such that we can compute a $1/k+\epsilon$ approximation for the longest common subsequence of $A$ and $B$ in $O(n^{2-\delta})$ time.
